caption: If your family needed to make a funeral claim, who would they call?
Would they know where to find the policy, who is covered, and what to do first?
Those are practical questions a family can answer while there is still time to plan.
This is Ayanda. Tonight, she and her mother are at the kitchen table, saving an important number and putting the family's documents into one folder.
This is where the EquiGrowth story begins.
In this film, we'll follow Ayanda as she explores funeral cover for her family, and Thandi, an appointed consultant, as she explains how EquiGrowth works and looks after the policies she services.
EquiGrowth is the public brand of MyEquiGrowth (Pty) Ltd.
It was established in 2024 as a Black empowerment company, built on relationships: with its clients, with its business partners, and within its own team.

Its founders describe a wider ambition to build wealth-building solutions with partners over time. That broader story is separate from the product in this film. Today, we are talking about one thing: funeral cover, and the people who service it.
EquiGrowth describes its strengths as five pillars. Rather than list them, let's watch them at work in an ordinary conversation.
Stewardship. When Ayanda asks a question Thandi can't answer on the spot, Thandi takes ownership of it, writes it down, and follows it through.
Integrity. Before she tells Ayanda who can be included, Thandi checks the policy detail instead of guessing.
A cohesive team. A colleague helps her find the right version of a document, so Ayanda gets one clear answer.
Continuous improvement. When customers say part of an explanation is confusing, the team rewrites it, and the next family has an easier time.
And quality service and support. Ayanda leaves with her paperwork in her hand, and she knows exactly whom to contact.
Now, an important question for any family: who actually stands behind the cover?
The name Ayanda sees is EquiGrowth. Behind the brand is the company, MyEquiGrowth (Pty) Ltd.
MyEquiGrowth is a juristic representative of Sibiya Brokers, a financial services provider, FSP 46798.
That means the financial services are provided under Sibiya Brokers' authorisation.
Anyone can check a financial services provider's status on the FSCA's public register.
EquiGrowth's partnership information also names the Mthembe Group, and it names RMA as the underwriter.
In everyday language, the underwriter is the insurer. It carries the risk that is covered, under the terms written in the policy.

So for Ayanda, these names answer three different questions. Who am I dealing with? Under whose financial services authorisation is the service provided? And which insurer stands behind the cover described in my policy?
Each answer belongs in her policy documents, so she never has to rely on memory.
EquiGrowth's revised offer is simple to describe: one funeral cover package, at R430 a month.
Every family on the package pays the same R430. The consultant's level makes no difference to the customer's price.
Thandi takes Ayanda through the questions a family should ask about any funeral policy.
First: who can be included on my policy? Thandi opens the policy schedule, and they check the list of insured people together.
Second: how much cover applies to each person? The schedule sets out the amount for each insured life. Thandi reads it from the document, not from memory or an older brochure.
Third: when does cover start, and which waiting periods or exclusions apply? Those are in the policy terms, and Thandi marks them so Ayanda can find them again.
And fourth: what should the family keep, and whom should they contact to claim? The claims contact goes into Ayanda's phone, and the schedule goes into the folder.
If an answer isn't clear on paper, the right response is: let me confirm that in writing. Never a guess.
Ayanda writes down one thing she wants confirmed, and Thandi notes it for follow-up. That is stewardship again, in practice.
Alongside the cover, EquiGrowth's presentation describes member benefits for everyday life.
These include grocery and pharmacy coupons, selected retail and airtime vouchers, travel and lifestyle discounts, and a home assistance service.
Thandi shows Ayanda which of these are attached to her package, according to her benefit schedule.
Before she shops, Ayanda checks that her grocery voucher is eligible and still valid. Then she uses it at the till.
When a pipe bursts at home, she calls the home assistance line, and the service arranges a qualified professional to come out.
Arranging help is not the same as paying the whole bill. What the service covers, and what Ayanda pays herself, is set out in the benefit terms.
The presentation also mentions a cashback benefit. The amount, what qualifies, and when it pays are details Ayanda should see in writing for her own package.
So here is the distinction worth remembering. The family receives the policy and the member benefits that apply to it. Consultant compensation is earned through a separate role.
Customers never need to recruit anyone, or become a consultant, to keep their cover or their benefits.
Joining starts at the website: myequigrowth.com.
Ayanda selects sign up and enters her own details: her name, her active mobile number and her email address.
She checks every field before she submits. Then she completes her profile, including her bank details for the monthly payment.
If anything on the form is unclear, the EquiGrowth office can help her complete it.
Ayanda saves her documents and contact details in the family folder. Her story as a customer is complete, whether or not she ever becomes a consultant.
Now, let's spend some time with Thandi.
Thandi is an appointed consultant. Before she could explain or arrange cover, the financial services provider confirmed what she is authorised to do.
A person can apply for appointment without buying the package, and nobody pays to unlock a level.
Her appointment comes with responsibilities: explaining the policy accurately, servicing the families she signs, and keeping their records in order.
EquiGrowth's revised system gives appointed consultants 13 portfolio milestones. A consultant progresses through the active, paid policies she personally sells and services.
Here is how the money works. One policy. One qualifying monthly payment. R80 allocated to the compensation pool.
A family on one policy counts once. If Ayanda's policy covers several family members, it is still one policy in Thandi's portfolio.
For every qualifying active policy paid that month, R80 is allocated to the compensation pool. The consultant's individual payment follows the agreed remuneration terms.
These are the 13 milestones.
At level 1, Thandi services 2 paid policies. 2 times R80 gives a monthly pool of R160.
At level 2, 4 policies: R320. At level 3, 8 policies: R640.
Each milestone doubles the number of policies. Levels 4 to 8 run from 16 policies to 256.
Levels 9 to 13 run from 512 policies up to 8,192.
Three things matter when you read this chart.
First, the milestones are snapshots of portfolio size. The amounts in different rows do not stack.
Second, every qualifying policy contributes R80, including the policies between milestones.
And third, the upper rows are arithmetic examples at those portfolio sizes. They don't mean that any one person will reach them, or personally receive the whole pool.
And throughout, the customer's package stays at R430 a month.
So what does this look like in a real month?
This month, Thandi personally services 10 qualifying paid policies. Here is her example statement.
10 times R430: R4,300 in customer payments.
10 times R80: R800 allocated to the monthly compensation pool.
That leaves R3,500 outside the allocation. How it is used depends on the actual product arrangements, including the insurance behind the cover.
Part of that amount has to fund the obligations behind the package, so none of it should be read as profit.
Thandi has passed the 8-policy milestone and is working towards 16. Her ninth and tenth policies still count.
Now meet Sipho, a separately appointed consultant who services 6 qualifying policies of his own. His portfolio generates its own pool of R480.
Thandi introduced Sipho to the company, but she receives no portfolio credit for his sales. Each consultant's figures come only from the families they personally serve.
So Thandi's statement grows only one way: by looking after more families, and looking after them well.
And through all of this, Ayanda still pays R430.
A policy is a relationship, not a single sale. Here is what service looks like after the policy is issued.
Thandi helps Ayanda find a document. She checks an administrative query. And when Ayanda asks about claims, Thandi directs her to the correct claims contact.
Later, Ayanda sits down with her mother and shows her the folder: the schedule, the claims contact, and the number saved in her phone.
The question from the beginning now has an answer. The family knows who to call.
Thandi's figures are calculated month by month. If 16 policies qualify in one month, the pool is R1,280. If 15 qualify the next month, it is R1,200.
What a missed payment means for a family's cover is set by the policy terms. That is a separate question from the consultant's monthly calculation.
If a policy is not paid in a month, it simply does not contribute to the pool that month.
So, what is the next step for you?
If you're here for your family, visit myequigrowth.com or speak to an appointed representative. Review who is covered, the benefits, the policy terms, and how to claim.
If you're interested in becoming a consultant, ask EquiGrowth for the appointment process, the service responsibilities, and the written remuneration terms.
Whichever path you are on, ask for the details in writing, and keep them in the folder.

For Ayanda, the important thing is knowing what her family has in place and who to call. For Thandi, it is knowing which families she serves, what each policy requires, and how her monthly figures are calculated.
That is how the revised EquiGrowth model fits together: one funeral cover package, supported by consultants who look after their own policyholders.
EquiGrowth. Empowering your financial journey.
